messages:
lee: Quick follow-up from the RFC — we need a practical rollout plan for cross-region token revocation and how it interacts with fairness shedding. Two options on the table: strong revocation (synchronous invalidate across regions) vs eventual revocation (async propagate). thoughts?

maria: My read: strong revocation gives better security guarantees but will add tail latency and complexity (coordination across regions). eventual is simpler but opens a short window where revoked tokens can still consume capacity.

jon: +1 to maria. Also worth thinking about the fairness scheduler: if a revoked tenant keeps consuming before propagation, our fair-share math will skew and penalize others. We could add a compensation pass to rebalance tokens after propagation.

lee: Yeah. Two tradeoffs I want to capture: 1) Safety window (how long we tolerate revocation lag) 2) Fairness correction (how we debit/compensate other tenants). Proposal: accept short eventual window (<= 5s), but immediately mark token as "revoked" in coordinator and emit a fast-path eviction hint to local workers. If worker still accepts, it should notify the lease service and the fairness engine applies retrospective crediting.

sophia: Implementation nit: workers have local LRU token caches. If we emit an eviction hint, workers need to invalidate the cache entry ASAP. But cross-region RTT means some will still have stale entries for a few ms. We should add a small per-tenant penalty budget to avoid radical oscillation. e.g., allow N inflight token usages to finish but charge them as "revoked-consumption" for billing/fairness.

jon: Can we outline the fast-path protocol? rough sketch:

```
1) Admin revokes token -> auth service marks token revocation time T and writes to central revocation log.
2) Coordinator pushes eviction hint to region broker (fanout).
3) Region broker marks local token as revoked and stops issuing new leases.
4) Existing leases with start < T are allowed to finish but flagged.
5) Fairness engine receives flagged events and adjusts tenant credits retrospectively.
```

maria: That seems fine. Questions: how do we ensure fairness adjustments don't open attack vectors? e.g., attacker might generate many short-lived requests to burn others' budgets before revocation hits.

lee: Good point. Mitigations: 1) rate-limit the number of retrospective credits applied per revocation window 2) maintain a sliding-window abuse score that raises scrutiny for tenants with suspicious burst patterns and reduces retrospective forgiveness 3) require higher-assurance revocation path for admin-initiated security revokes (force-kill) which does synchronous disconnects for the most critical cases.

infra-bot: Deploy-checklist: rolling rollout plan recommended. Start with non-prod region, enable "eviction_hint" log-only for 48h, surface metrics: propagation latency, number of flagged leases, fairness-adjustment delta.

lee: Action items: jon to add compensation pseudocode + metrics to RFC, sophia to draft worker cache invalidation patch, maria to enumerate abuse heuristics. I'll coordinate the staged rollout with infra-bot checklist.

maria: ack. I'll also write a test harness simulating cross-region revocations and verify fairness deltas stay within 1-2% on our synthetic workloads.

jon: I'll put the pseudocode in the RFC by EOD. quick Q: what should the default revocation window be? 5s? 2s?

sophia: Start with 5s in prod flags, can tighten to 2s after we see propagation stable.

lee: cool — thanks everyone. tagging follow-ups in the RFC thread. :thumbsup:
